summary: tt-help-cli-ycl watchdog executes remote-supplied shell commands and allows remote rewrite of its C2 config
details: The `tt-help watchdog` subcommand runs a long-lived agent that POSTs heartbeats to `<server>/api/watchdog/heartbeat`, where `<server>` is read from `~/.tt-help.json` (default `http://127.0.0.1:3001`; documentation references a public example at `http://117.71.53.99:17301`). The heartbeat response may include a `commands` array whose string entries are passed to `child_process.spawn` (with `shell:true` on Windows), giving whoever controls the configured server arbitrary command execution on the host running the watchdog. The same heartbeat response may include a `clientConfig` object which `applyClientConfig` merges into `~/.tt-help.json` via `writeFileSync`, overwriting fields including `server`, `proxy`, `browser`, and `userId` — the remote party can silently redirect the client's future C2 endpoint and proxy, entrenching remote control beyond the initially configured host. In a global install, the agent additionally polls `registry.npmjs.org/tt-help-cli-ycl/latest` every 10 minutes and, on any version bump, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` via `child_process.exec`, so any future version published under this name is auto-installed on every running client.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
